02 — TNF-α (conditional binder) · the complete history

This document tells the whole story of the TNF-alpha conditional-binder campaign, from the first failure analysis to the submitted eight designs. It names every tool, every decision, and the reason for each. The companion records are lineage.json (the site's own history), notes/ (the research and the evidence tables), and submission/ (what was actually uploaded).

Status: submitted 2026-10-18, eight designs, submission 1 on Proteinbase marked DESIGNATED. No wet-lab data exists for any design here; everything below is computational evidence.

1. The target and the three objectives

The brief ranks three objectives, in this order (the previous README, notes/master-plan.md):

  1. pH-selective binding: bind human TNF-alpha at pH 7.4, with no detectable binding at pH 6.0. The direction is inverted relative to challenge 1 — the binder is meant to let go in the acidifying endosome so it can be recycled rather than consumed.
  2. Mouse cross-reactivity, measured at pH 7.4 — the same molecule must also hold the mouse protein, so the design can be tested in mice.
  3. Affinity — bind strongly.

The recommended epitope in the brief is the receptor-binding site at the interface between two protomers of the TNF-alpha trimer (PDB 1TNF).

All three objectives had to land on one molecule. That is the whole difficulty: each objective pulls the sequence in a different direction, and a design that wins any one of them alone is worth nothing here.

2. The biology in plain words

What TNF-alpha is. TNF-alpha is a signalling protein the immune system releases to start inflammation. Too much of it drives rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease and psoriasis; the biggest-selling drugs of the last two decades (adalimumab, infliximab) are antibodies that mop it up.

Why it is a trimer. The active form is three identical copies of the same protein locked together into a cone — a trimer. The three copies are called protomers. The receptors it activates sit in the grooves between protomers, so the functional surfaces of TNF-alpha are seams, not faces. A binder aimed at such a seam has to touch two protomers at once. This is not a detail: the released campaign's own wet-lab winners all did exactly that ("every winner's contact list we checked (6 of 13) spans two or three target chains", notes/filter-calibration.md), and the at-site screen used throughout this campaign requires the two halves of the epitope to be touched on different protomers.

What "pH 7.4 bind, pH 6.0 release" means physically. Blood and the space between cells sit at about pH 7.4. When a cell swallows something, the bubble it swallows it in (the endosome) is deliberately acidified, down to about pH 6.0 and lower. A binder that holds at 7.4 and lets go at 6.0 therefore releases its cargo inside the cell and can be carried back out and reused. The chemistry that makes this possible is almost always histidine. Of the twenty amino acids, histidine is the only one whose charge flips in this exact window: near-neutral at pH 7.4, positively charged at pH 6.0. Put a histidine on the binder facing a positively charged residue on the target, and you get a switch: neutral at 7.4, so the binder holds; positive at 6.0, so two positive charges push each other apart and the binder leaves. That one sentence is the mechanism behind every switch design in this campaign (submission/methodology.md, notes/linkage-check.md).

Why mouse cross-reactivity is hard. Human and mouse TNF-alpha are similar but not identical. Where the sequences differ inside the designed contact patch, a binder tuned on one species can fail on the other. The phase-0 measurement found both a safe case and a trap (notes/research-phase-0.md):

residue human mouse consequence
103 Arg Lys both positive — charge class kept, safe for a switch
112 Lys Lys identical — safe
73 His Tyr charge class lost — a switch built here works on human only

The practical finding came later and was blunter: cross-reactivity has to be selected for, not checked for. The first family kept the designed interface on mouse but at roughly 0.2 lower interface confidence (lineage.json, chapter mouse-check), and the fix was to reverse the order of work — fold against mouse first, confirm on human second.

What is actually being measured here. Nothing in this project measures binding. Everything is a structure prediction and a score computed from it. The main number, ipSAE, answers "does the prediction put a confident interface between these two chains". It does not answer "will this stick in a tube". Chapter 4 is about what that distinction cost.

3. The reference structures and the released dataset

1TNF (inputs/1TNF.cif, data/epitope-analysis/1TNF.pdb) — the crystal structure of the human TNF-alpha trimer, and the target file for every generation run. A crystal structure is a map of where every atom sits, worked out by firing X-rays through a grid of billions of aligned copies of the molecule. It is one frozen pose, not a movie.

3WD5 and 4G3Y (data/epitope-analysis/) — TNF-alpha caught in the grip of the two approved antibody drugs, adalimumab and infliximab. These were used to locate a real, functionally validated epitope on the trimer (the "antibody groove"), and as the source of the S1 hotspot set.

2TNF (inputs/2TNF.cif) — a second TNF-alpha crystal form, kept as an input.

The construct, exactly. Every fold in the campaign used the same chains: the human construct P01375 82–233 and the mouse construct P06804 85–235 (handoff/README.md, submission/design-method.md). Two facts about it are recorded because they would otherwise silently break comparisons: the 1TNF construct differs from the UniProt sequence at one position (1TNF 219 is Leu, the UniProt residue is Asp), and all folds must use the same construct or the numbers are not comparable (handoff/README.md). The mouse target was built by aligning human 82–233 onto mouse 85–235; the designed site remaps to positions 107 and 67 (lineage.json, chapter mouse-check). Note that inputs/human_tnf.fasta is labelled P01375 77–233 — a wider slice than the 82–233 the fold records name; the fold YAMLs are the authority for what was folded.

The released campaign — the single most valuable asset in this challenge. Anthropic published a TNF-alpha binder-design dataset (Anthropic/claude-protein-binder-design, CC BY 4.0): 150 designs with real wet-lab outcomes from two labs, plus in-silico metrics from nine predictor arms including ipsae_min_boltz2 — the same metric family used here. That dataset turned "pick a threshold and hope" into a calibration problem with an answer key. Chapter 4 is what it said.

What was measured on the trimer directly (our own script, reported in notes/research-phase-0.md):

what was looked at what was found
can one binder reach the cation trio CA–CA spans A103–B103 10.7 Å, A103–B112 8.7 Å, B103–B112 12.9 Å — all under 13 Å, inside the ~15 Å one binder can span
is the trio's neighbourhood clean no: the nearest acidic side chains are 3.1–4.7 Å away (B104/Glu, C104/Glu), and they are also the affinity anchors — a binder histidine aimed at a cation can be screened by them
how polar the antibody groove is very (3–15% apolar) — expect a charged interface, which suits a salt-bridge switch but needs explicit polar contacts

One number did not reconcile and is recorded as an open item: a published baseline quotes a 20.2 Å maximum span for its version of the switch trio, while all three of our pairs sit under 13 Å (notes/research-phase-0.md).

4. The doctrine: calibrate the filters before trusting them

This campaign made two calibration moves before design work, and both changed the outcome.

4.1 Calibrating the acceptance bar against real wet-lab results

The original bar was ipSAE_min >= 0.6 AND pDockQ2 >= 0.23 — the AlphaFold-DB style default, set without ever having seen a known binder. Re-scoring the released campaign fixed it (notes/filter-calibration.md, 2026-10-16):

ipsae_min_boltz2 bucket bound / n win rate
≥ 0.8 9 / 35 25.7 %
0.7 – 0.8 3 / 30 10.0 %
0.6 – 0.7 0 / 22 0 %
0.4 – 0.6 0 / 20 0 %
< 0.4 1 / 36 2.8 %

The 0.6–0.7 band bound nothing in 22 attempts. So 0.6 became a "do not discard" floor and 0.8 became the submission line. The base rate across all 150 designs was 8.7 %.

The same dataset answered a bigger question — which generator to use:

generator bound / n win rate
Genie 3 8 / 23 34.8 %
PXDesign 4 / 57 7.0 %
RFdiffusion3 1 / 40 2.5 %
RFdiffusion 0 / 20 0 %
BoltzGen 0 / 8 0 %
BindCraft 0 / 2 0 %

The generator in use at that moment was the 2.5 % one. That single table is why the whole campaign was restarted on Genie 3.

Six released designs were then folded through our own pipeline as an instrument check (notes/calibration/fold-scores.csv):

design lab outcome our ipSAE our pDockQ2 their ipSAE
rank05 (Genie 3) binder, KD 4.2 nM, mouse+ 0.901 0.283 0.878
rank15 (PXDesign) binder, KD 0.70 nM 0.863 0.245 0.907
rank02 (Genie 3) binder, KD 2.1 nM, mouse+ 0.269 0.068 0.057
loser Mythos r08 non-binder 0.906 0.567 0.920
loser Mythos r03 non-binder 0.910 0.506 0.895
loser Mythos r04 non-binder 0.894 0.490 0.895

Three verdicts came out of that table, and all three were obeyed for the rest of the campaign:

  • the pipeline is correct — our numbers reproduce theirs within ±0.03;
  • a high score is not a promise — three never-bound designs outscored every winner, and their pDockQ2 (0.49–0.57) sat far above every winner's (0.07–0.28). pDockQ2 was therefore reported but never used as a gate, because it is non-discriminative on this target;
  • a low score is not a disqualification — a genuine 2.1 nM mouse-cross-reactive binder scores 0.06 in their table and 0.269 in ours. The metric is rank-grade, not a measurement.

A fourth finding set the design strategy: of the three mouse-cross-reactive binders in that dataset, human affinities were 2.1 / 4.2 / 18.9 nM, and nothing weaker than 19 nM bound mouse at all. Cross-reactivity arrives with tightness.

4.2 Calibrating where the interface is — the site rule

The second calibration is the finding this challenge contributed to every later challenge in the repo (notes/campaign-close.md, notes/x3-strategy.md):

ipSAE answers "is there an interface here", not "is the interface where the design put it".

The evidence, measured on the earlier track's own folds:

  • its single "passing" fold (ipSAE 0.733) sits 15–18 Å from the groove it was designed for; the samples that do land on the groove score at most 0.433;
  • across the X3 folds, the 9 samples that sit on their designed epitope score 0.000, while the batch's highest score (0.769) sits 18 Å away;
  • the fold model has favourite surfaces of its own — the drug groove (K65/Q67/E110) and the receptor-binding loops (R31/A33, Y84–91, A145–S147) — and it prefers them over whatever patch the design program was aimed at.

Consequence, enforced from then on: selection requires score AND site together. The check is handoff/scripts/screen_folds_site.py, and in the Genie 3 campaign it is the at_site / cross columns of notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv: a sample counts only if the binder touches both halves of the epitope and does so on two different protomers.

A third, smaller calibration rule came from the same period and stayed in force: the full-trimer loophole check — any design with atoms where a missing protomer would sit is discarded whatever it scores (notes/master-plan.md, stop rule 4).

5. The closed track: the third-party pipeline, and why it was replaced

Before the submitted campaign existed there was a different one. It is closed, it produced no submitted design, and it is in this document because its negatives are the reason the second attempt worked. The full post-mortem is notes/campaign-close.md; the engines and upstream snapshot it used were removed from this tree on 2026-11-08, so every file here is our own work.

The track's own stage table (notes/campaign-close.md):

stage designs result
X1 — BoltzGen, three hotspot sets (Tamarind) 150 0 docked, best ipSAE ≈ 0.005
X2 — RFdiffusion3, the drug groove (Tamarind) 72 one fold cleared the bar — at a different site
W2 — the 8-design shortlist, local GPU 8 best ipSAE 0.733, again off-site
X3-A/B/C — local RFD3 on three patches 72 0 that clear the bar and sit on the designed patch
X3-D — the patch the fold model prefers 96 0 of 6 folded, same result

Total: 18 designs co-folded, 90 predicted samples, zero samples that clear the bar and sit on the designed epitope.

What each stage actually taught:

  • X1 (notes/x1-results.md) answered the hotspot question and closed it. Best design→target ipTM 0.356, best ipSAE 0.005, pDockQ2 0.000 across all three sets — and the no-hotspot diagnostic set did no better than the targeted ones. So the site choice was not the limiter. The top designs press against the trimer (162 of 639 binder atoms within 4 Å) with essentially zero interface confidence: "touching, not docking". Meanwhile the trimer's own internal interfaces scored 0.30–0.44 — the model predicts the target fine; it is the designed interface that is absent. Pre-registered stop rule 1 fired.
  • X2 (notes/x2-results.md) was the generator swap, and it worked as placement: RFdiffusion3 put 72 of 72 designs on the 60s loop and 58 of 72 across the groove spanning two protomers. One independent Boltz-2 co-fold passed the bar in 1 of 5 samples (ipSAE 0.804, ipSAE_min 0.606, pDockQ2 0.236); one sample was near, one partial, and two lost the interface entirely. Recorded as a qualified positive with seed variance as the caveat. 27 of the 72 raw designs had physically impossible geometry (minimum heavy-atom distance under 2.0 Å, worst 0.34 Å) — raw diffusion output needs screening.
  • W2 (notes/w2-fold-triage.md) folded the eight-design shortlist against human and mouse. One design (groove-1_0_model_1, 73 aa) reached ipSAE 0.733 human / 0.810 mouse; no design cleared both halves of the bar; six of eight stayed under 0.45 and two showed no interface at all. It also recorded an uncomfortable fact honestly: that design folds onto mouse better than human, which for a human-selective design is the wrong direction — logged as a risk, not a pass.
  • X3 (notes/x3-strategy.md) changed both the epitope and the target representation. The patch map ranked the real TNFR-binding surface (the 84–89 and 143–148 loops) above anything X1/X2 had targeted, and the key measurement was that pairing one protomer's loop with its neighbour's turns an impossible 35–49 Å span into a feasible 15.3 Å one — set X3-A = A83, A87, A89, B147. Trimming the target from 456 residues/~3600 atoms to 195/1543 cut generation from 302 s to 50 s per design and GPU memory from 11.88 to 8.8 GiB. Generation then behaved: 24/24 designs at the switch trio, 21/24 at the X2 groove (the control that tied the local box to the validated Tamarind run), 11/24 at the receptor site. And the folds still refused: best scores 0.012–0.230, none at the bar.

Four bugs found on the way, each of which cost real time or produced a wrong number (notes/campaign-close.md):

  1. IPSAE names its report after the model file, not the PAE file — copying Boltz outputs under new names silently drops the pLDDT file and pDockQ2 collapses to a floor value (0.0073 instead of 0.1325) while ipSAE stays right.
  2. infer_ori_strategy must be hotspots for binder design. Without it the diffusion origin comes from the structure's centre of mass and the binder is generated inside the target: 12 designs had 24–61 atoms under 2 Å of the target. After the fix: 0–2 atoms.
  3. A contig range must not skip a residue — a trimmed target needs its contig built from the surviving blocks (handoff/rfd3/make_patch.py) or RFD3 aborts.
  4. A site check keyed by set name against per-design folders silently passes everything: every fold was scored against an empty site map and reported "no contact" until the map was matched by prefix.

Decision. On the pre-registered rule ("if W2 fails, stop the campaign track and record the negative") the track was closed on 2026-10-16. Nothing from it was submitted. Its two transfers were the site rule and the pitfall list.

6. The pipeline, stage by stage

This is the pipeline that produced the submission: one methodology throughout — Genie 3 → ProteinMPNN → Boltz-2 → IPSAE, with PROPKA bolted on for the pH layer.

The whole pipeline as a funnel: 36 Genie 3 backbones in three batches, 234 unique sequences designed on them, 1,370 Boltz-2 samples scored, and the eight designs that were submitted. Green chips are free CPU steps measured in seconds, orange chips cost GPU minutes on the 12 GB local card, and the pink chip is the post-submission verification round. The note at the bottom shows the loops that fed new variants back in — two evolution generations, two dual-species generations, two mining rounds and the switch recovery scan; none of them is machine learning, nothing is trained, and every child is judged by the same fold-and-score instruments.

Stage 1 — Generation (Genie 3). Hypothesis: the generator choice dominates everything else, and the released-campaign calibration names Genie 3. Procedure: Genie 3 (aqlaboratory, 347 MB checkpoint, Apache-2.0), run on the released BinderBench problem 10_tnfa — hotspots B102 + D62, two residues on two different protomers, binder length 50–120. Numbers (notes/genie3-feasibility.md): 8 designs in 525 s (66 s each), peak 2.43 GiB host memory, about 4.5 GB GPU; a 100-design batch would take about 1.8 h. Placement: 8 of 8 designs engage the designed interface (CA–CA 4.3–8.1 Å to the hotspots, 18–32 target residues within 10 Å). Decision: the generator is usable and reliable at placement; it was never the problem again. Three batches were generated in all — batch-01 (8), batch-02 (16) and an RBS batch-03 (12) on our own receptor-site junction.

Stage 2 — Sequence design, and the trap that nearly ended the campaign. Hypothesis: ProteinMPNN can write a sequence for a generated backbone. What went wrong: the first pass ran ProteinMPNN on CA atoms only (the generator's own default setting, since Genie 3 emits CA traces). Every sequence produced that way capped at 0.248 at-site ipSAE — ten of the fourteen at-site samples scored exactly 0.000 (notes/genie3-feasibility.md). The best score in the whole 40-fold batch was 0.252, and it was off-site. The fix: re-sequence the folded backbone — which has a full backbone, not just CA positions — with full-backbone ProteinMPNN (vanilla v_48_020). Numbers after the fix (notes/genie3-round2-family.md): the same d7 backbone went from capped-at-0.248 to 18 members spanning 0.63–0.85, every sequence's five folds at the designed site. That one change is the difference between this campaign and its predecessor.

Stage 3 — Pick backbones by their folded spread, not by their scores. Hypothesis: backbone quality dominates sequence quality, so backbones should be selected before sequences are expanded. Evidence: control backbone d6 stayed at or below 0.19 under identical full-backbone treatment, while d7 produced a whole family; d15 produced interfaces of 373–551 atom pairs — larger than any released winner — at only 0.47–0.69, showing that more contact is not more confidence (notes/genie3-round2-family.md). Decision: read the backbone's at-site fold spread first; expand only the backbones that reproduce. Two families survived: d7 (64 residues) and d12 (92 residues).

Stage 4 — Co-folding (Boltz-2). Every candidate is co-folded with the target construct: 5 diffusion samples, seed 42, Boltz-2 2.2.1, MSA server, on the local RTX 5070 (12 GB), under a 12.5 GB memory cap. Cost about 3.5 min per design (3 min of it MSA). The fold is treated as a distribution: the champion's whole five-sample spread is reported, never a single lucky sample. Over the campaign this produced 1,370 samples across 274 designs (notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv).

Stage 5 — The at-site screen (IPSAE). ipSAE at a 10 Å PAE cutoff, plus the site rule from chapter 4: the binder must contact both halves of the epitope, on two different protomers. Script: screen_all.py (working tree). The bar: ipSAE ≥ 0.8 to submit, 0.6 as the do-not-discard floor; pDockQ2 recorded but not gating. Of the 1,370 samples, 896 sit at the designed site; of those, 279 score in the 0.6–0.8 band and 227 score ≥ 0.8 (the remaining 390 are at site but below the floor).

Stage 6 — Mouse-first selection. Hypothesis (initially wrong): a design selected on human will be checked on mouse and will hold. Numbers: it did not. The family's champions kept the designed interface on mouse but roughly 0.2 lower (notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv, the mc-* rows):

design human at-site ipSAE mouse at-site ipSAE
d7x-t3-3 0.852 (5/5) 0.636 (5/5)
e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6 0.871 (5/5) 0.632 (5/5)
m1-d7b-3 0.825 (5/5) 0.770 (3/5)
b2x-d12-2 0.788 (5/5) 0.426 (5/5)
d7x-t3-1 0.826 (5/5) 0.258 (3/5)

For reference, the released campaign's three mouse-cross-reactive winners folded through the same pipeline against mouse read 0.886 (rank05), 0.867 (rank03) and 0.218 (rank02 — the known metric outlier, a real 2.1 nM binder that scores near zero in every tool). Decision: reverse the order. From that point candidates are folded against mouse first, and only mouse survivors earn a human confirmation fold.

Stage 7 — The pH layer (PROPKA + the Wyman linkage). Every complex is scored for delta_log_Ka — the change in binding strength over the 6.0→7.4 window, computed from PROPKA pKa predictions through the Wyman linkage relation (tools/switch/linkage_score.py in the working tree; the metric is documented in tools/insights.py). Positive means binding is favoured at pH 7.4 — the direction this challenge wants. The sign is the decision variable; the magnitude is rank-grade only.

Stage 8 — Selection and controls. Designs are ranked on the three objectives together, and every switch design is submitted with its no-switch parent — the same binder with the histidine removed — so that whatever the lab sees between a pair is the switch and nothing else (submission/methodology.md).

7. The campaigns and experiments

Two campaigns are on record in lineage.json. The first is the negative; the second is fourteen experiments under one methodology. The per-experiment texts below follow that file; the numbers are cross-checked against notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv and notes/calibration/*.csv.

7.1 C2 campaign — RFdiffusion3 (2026-10-15 → 16) · verdict: negative

Tools: RFdiffusion3, Boltz-2, IPSAE. 40 backbones across two batches (w1, w2) around the B102/D62 junction and the human groove; each candidate co-folded with the human construct at 5 samples, seed 42, on the local GPU; scored with IPSAE at a 10 Å cutoff against the bar ipSAE >= 0.6 AND pDockQ2 >= 0.23. Result: 0 of 18 designs cleared the bar at the designed site. Good whole-complex ipTM (0.92–0.96), weak interfaces. Closed 2026-10-16 as a documented negative, with two lessons: generator choice dominates (Genie 3 8/23 versus RFdiffusion3 1/40 in the calibration) and the acceptance line belongs at 0.8. This campaign is the lineage-level record of the track described in chapter 5; its designs stay in the table with their scores rather than being discarded.

7.2 Genie 3 campaign — the night run (2026-10-17 → 18) · verdict: record

279 design records, 234 unique binder sequences, 1,370 folds, from the first 0.25 to the submission set. Fourteen experiments:

Calibration — the bars (10-16; Boltz-2, IPSAE). The released-dataset work of chapter 4: ipSAE 0.8 as the submission line, 0.6 as the do-not-discard floor, pDockQ2 0.23 reported not gated, reproducibility within ±0.03. Outcome: bars fixed before generation.

Generation — Genie 3 (10-17; Genie 3). 8 designs on problem 10_tnfa, all 8 on the designed interface; CA-only ProteinMPNN sequences capped at 0.248. Outcome: the first families land around 0.25 at-site ipSAE — and the CA-only trap is identified.

The d7 family (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2, IPSAE). Chain A of the d7 fold becomes the template; full-backbone ProteinMPNN at T = 0.1 and 0.3 over several seeds gives 18 variants. Champion d7x-t3-3: five independent folds read 0.832 / 0.837 / 0.840 / 0.842 / 0.852, all 5/5 at site, 209 interface atom pairs. Fresh sampling reproduced it — 9 of 10 new sequences landed 0.75–0.85 at site, so the family is not one lucky draw. For scale, the released real binders read 0.86–0.91 through this same protocol. Outcome: d7 is the working scaffold.

Directed evolution (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2, IPSAE). Fixed-position ProteinMPNN around the champions, 3 mutable positions per variant. Generation 1: 24 variants; e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6 = the champion plus ONE substitution (D47A) → 0.871, the project's human record. Generation 2 converged: nothing beat v6 (best child 0.863). Two setup bugs (the mutation template, and one-letter residue codes) were caught by the validation gate before any fold was spent (notes/lineage-best-design.md). Outcome: v6 heads the ladder at human 0.871 / mouse 0.632.

Mouse check + calibration (10-17; Boltz-2, IPSAE). The table in stage 6 above. Outcome: the species gap measured; cross-reactivity must be selected for.

Mouse-directed redesign (mce) (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2). 64 ProteinMPNN sequences on the same d7 backbone, re-sequenced toward the mouse-conserved contacts; the 16 best-predicted folded against mouse. One hit: mce-14 — mouse 0.847 (5/5), human 0.852 (5/5), 78 % identical to d7x-t3-3 (50 of 64 positions), i.e. a genuinely different sequence on the same backbone rather than a point mutant. A Mol visual check confirmed it hugs the trimer the same way on both species (notes/views-review-mce14.md). Outcome: the first dual-species hit.*

Dual-select generation 1 (ds) (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2). Selection pressure on both species at once: mouse stage first (all five mce-14 mutants held mouse at 0.839–0.863), then a human confirmation stage (all six promoted designs 5/5 at site). ds-mce-14-v6 = mce-14 + T48S: mouse 0.854 / human 0.856 — better than its parent on both targets. Outcome: the submission head.

Dual-select generation 2 (ds2) (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2, Mol). 8 of 9 mutants at or above 0.847 on mouse; ds2-mce-14-v7-v1 set the mouse record at 0.868 (human 0.824). But no design beat ds-mce-14-v6's combined profile. Outcome: the family has plateaued; ds2-mce-14-v7-v1 is kept for the ladder.*

pH linkage check — the missing objective (10-17; PROPKA 3.5.1). The first time the top-ranked objective was measured on the lineage, and the answer was bad (notes/linkage-check.md):

design delta_log_Ka fold selectivity sites
ds-mce-14-v6 (human) −0.113 0.8 2
v6 (human) −0.167 0.7 1
ds-mce-14-v6 (mouse) −0.712 0.2 2
ds-mce-14-v7 (mouse) −0.946 0.1 3
mce-14 (mouse) −0.991 0.1 4

Every design binds more in acid — the lineage did not merely lack a switch, its natural linkage ran the wrong way, 1.3–1.4× on human targets and 5–10× on mouse. Objective 1 was unclaimable, and the design would likely fail "no detectable binding at pH 6.0" outright. Outcome: a recorded negative, and a named retrofit to attempt.

The switch — histidine retrofit and E33H (10-18; PROPKA 3.5.1, ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2). The campaign's decisive experiment, in four moves (notes/lineage-best-design.md, notes/calibration/sr*.csv):

  1. Round 1 (sr1) — the sign flips. Nine histidine mutants on the dual backbones. The strongest read +0.877 (7.5×) — but the variant that also survived the mouse fold was the b-class, sr1-mce-14-b (mce-14 + L37H + L43H + G45H): human 0.659 / mouse 0.703, both 5/5, switch +0.836 (6.9×). The histidines cost roughly 0.15–0.2 of binding confidence.
  2. Recovery (sr3/sr4). Whole-chain resampling to buy the binding back collapsed on these backbones — recorded as a negative.
  3. Reversion scan (sr6). Reverting the histidines one at a time localised the binding cost to H37. sr6-r37 (the b-class with position 37 back to Leu) reads human 0.811 / mouse 0.872 — the project's best mouse score — with a much weaker switch, +0.169 (1.5×).
  4. Alternative positions (sr2) — the winner. A scan of histidine sites 7–9 Å from the interface cations, away from the binding face. E33H alone — converting a glutamate that forms a salt bridge to a conserved interface lysine into a histidine — gave sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2c: human 0.849, mouse 0.847 (both 5/5 at the designed junction), switch +1.738 = 54.7× toward pH 7.4, against its parent's −0.113. All three objectives on one molecule, at the cost of 0.007 of human confidence.

Outcome in lineage.json: "sr1 carries the engineered linkage; the pH objective stays open" — i.e. the mechanism is engineered and scored, not demonstrated.

The d12 family — second scaffold (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2). 16 designs from batch-02, re-sequenced full-backbone: 0.62–0.83, every sequence 5/5 at the designed leg, and b2x-d12-2 buries 311 atom pairs — winner scale. It is also the only family that passed the old pDockQ2 leg (0.20–0.30, versus d7's 0.08–0.16). But the mouse verdict killed it: b2x-d12-2 reads human 0.788 / mouse 0.426. Outcome: a second working scaffold, human-context only; the d7 lineage carries the dual objective.

Mining-01 — the d7 plateau (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2; pre-registered). 80 further sequences across both backbones and three temperatures, 20 folded. Best new design 0.837 — under the 0.85 of the incumbent. m1-d7b-3 (0.825) and m1-d7a-4 (0.804) joined the ladder. Outcome: the family ceiling measured.

Mining-02 — fresh backbones (10-17; ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2; pre-registered). The four best untreated backbones from both Genie 3 batches, vanilla MPNN, top six sequences folded each (24 folds). Best 0.599 at site (5/5) — a near-miss. Outcome: no third family; the family space in both batches is closed.

RBS batch-03 + redesign (10-17; Genie 3, ProteinMPNN, Boltz-2). The receptor-binding-site junction (1TNF file residues 84–89 + 143–148, a custom problem JSON reusing the released target files) retried under the now-fixed protocol. Genie 3 placed 3 of 12 designs on both junction halves with winner-scale contact counts, but all twelve CA-only folds read 0.000–0.438, and full-backbone redesigns of the three best backbones (18 more folds) stayed at 0.000–0.653 — with the high scorers moved off the junction. Outcome: the RBS negative holds even under the fixed protocol. Epitope difficulty gates the fix.

7.3 One lineage, in one line

Genie 3 (10_tnfa) → d7 backbone → full-backbone ProteinMPNN
  → d7x-t3-3 (0.852) → D47A → e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6 (human record 0.871)
d7 backbone → mouse-directed re-sequencing → mce-14 (first dual hit)
  → T48S → ds-mce-14-v6 (0.856 / 0.854) → ds2 (mouse record 0.868)
  → sr1 histidine retrofit → sr2 alternative positions → E33H
  → sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2c (0.849 / 0.847, switch +1.738)

All eight submitted designs are 64 residues and all eight descend from the same Genie 3 backbone, d7. The full ancestry with the mermaid diagram is notes/lineage-best-design.md.

Three members of the single surviving lineage, each on the human TNF-alpha trimer (the three protomers in blue, cyan and gray; the binder in magenta). Each panel is that design's own Boltz-2 fold, its best at-site sample - not a shared frame, so the poses are comparable only in the sense that each is self-consistent. Left: e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6, the human record (0.871) that could not hold mouse. Centre: ds-mce-14-v6, the dual-species head (0.856 human / 0.854 mouse) and the paired no-switch control. Right: sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2c, the same binder with one substitution (E33H) that adds the pH switch. In every panel the binder lies along the seam where two protomers meet — the geometry the at-site screen enforces.

8. Every tool, when and why

tool role when why
Genie 3 (aqlaboratory, 347 MB ckpt) backbone generation the submitted campaign the released calibration's best generator by win rate (8/23); fast (66 s/design) and reliable at placement (8/8 on-epitope)
ProteinMPNN (v_48_020) sequence design every experiment after generation inverse folding; full-backbone mode is mandatory (CA-only caps at 0.248)
ProteinMPNN fixed-position mode directed evolution and dual-select evolution, ds, ds2, sr 3 free positions per variant — single-substitution steps that can be attributed
Boltz-2 2.2.1 co-folding, all interface reads everywhere the workhorse oracle; 5 samples, seed 42, 12.5 GB cap, ~3.5 min/design
IPSAE (Dunbrack) interface scoring from PAE everywhere ipSAE_min was the best single predictor of lab binding in the 2025 meta-analysis of 3,766 designs
screen_all.py / screen_folds_site.py the at-site screen everywhere score alone selects interfaces anywhere on the target; site + score together is the rule
PROPKA 3.5.1 + linkage_score.py pH linkage (delta_log_Ka) the switch work the only instrument in the stack that reads objective 1 at all
Mol* (molstar_views.py), headless Chromium viewpoint renders, visual review mce/v6 review, viewers checks the pose a score cannot show
released Anthropic dataset calibration before generation the bars, the generator choice, the mouse-tightness link
RFdiffusion3 backbone generation the closed track (X2, X3) replaced; 1/40 in the calibration
BoltzGen 0.3.2 generation (X1), then re-scoring X1; the 10-20 verification 0/150 docked as a generator; useful later as an independent scorer
Tamarind Bio (free tier) hosted runs of BoltzGen/RFD3/Boltz-2 X1, X2 the only route to BoltzGen (24 GB floor, local card has 12); 10 jobs/month, fully spent
memlimit.py, watch_resources.py resource caps and logging every local job the Windows host crashed twice under load; caps became mandatory

Not used, and why. BindCraft (PyRosetta licence, 0/2 in the calibration); original RFdiffusion (no Blackwell kernels); Proton-PottsMPNN — protonation-aware sequence design, which sounds ideal here, but its transitions only reach pH 4.0–5.8, below the 6.0–7.4 window this challenge needs (notes/research-phase-0.md).

The hardware, correctly. The plans assumed an RTX 5070 Ti with 16 GB; the machine turned out to be an RTX 5070 with 12 227 MiB (notes/pc-session-1.md, notes/gpu-box-setup.md). Boltz-2 needs about 11.3 GiB of host memory for a 4-chain ~540-residue complex and none of the usual levers reduced it, so the WSL VM was raised from 12 GB to 16 GB, after which folds peak at 7.6 GiB and run at full speed (notes/x3-strategy.md).

9. How the designs were evaluated, and how "better" was decided

The rules were fixed before the designs existed (notes/research-phase-0.md for the bands, notes/filter-calibration.md for the bars, notes/master-plan.md for the stop rules).

Step 1 — the score bar. ipSAE at a 10 Å PAE cutoff, read on the binder→target interface. ≥ 0.8 submit · 0.6–0.8 possible · < 0.6 discard. pDockQ2 recorded (≥ 0.23 was the old second leg) but not gating, because the calibration showed it non-discriminative on this target — the released non-binders scored 0.49–0.57 against the winners' 0.07–0.28.

Step 2 — the site rule. A sample counts only if the binder contacts both halves of the designed epitope and does so on two different protomers. Scores and sites are reported together (at_site, cross in notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv).

Step 3 — the spread, not the sample. Five Boltz-2 samples per design; the champion's whole spread is reported, and designs are compared on best-at-site with the at-site count beside it (5/5, 3/5, …). A design whose interface appears in 1 of 5 samples is not treated as a design that binds — that was precisely the earlier track's error.

Step 4 — the species order. Mouse first, human second. A design that does not hold on mouse is removed before a human fold is considered (submission/design-method.md).

Step 5 — the switch sign. delta_log_Ka > 0 is required for a switch design. The sign is the decision variable; the magnitude ranks within the sign.

Step 6 — one substitution at a time. Evolution and dual-select steps move 3 positions at most, so every gain is attributable: D47A bought +0.019 human; T48S bought both species; E33H bought +1.851 of linkage for −0.007 human.

Step 7 — paired controls. Every switch design is submitted together with its no-switch parent, so the lab measures the switch and not the scaffold.

Step 8 — stop rules and diversity. The pre-registered stop rules (notes/master-plan.md): stop the track if nothing docks in any hotspot set; do not scale a setup whose pass rate is below 1 %; discard any design that violates the full-trimer loophole check whatever it scores; cap at two designs per backbone.

What "better" explicitly did not mean. Not the highest linkage score: sr2-ds-mce-14-v6-r2b reads +2.07 (117.6×) — the strongest switch the project ever measured — and was not submitted, because its binding collapsed: best ipSAE 0.722 with only 1 of 5 samples at the designed site (notes/calibration/sr2-ranked.csv, notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv). The same reasoning dropped the sr1 c-class (+0.877, the strongest round-1 switch) because it lost mouse. Objective 1 ranks first in the brief, but a switch on a molecule that does not bind is worth nothing.

10. How the design serves objective 1: the pH switch

Three ways the campaign placed the switch on the same 64-residue scaffold, each shown on the human trimer. Left: sr1-mce-14-b, three histidines (L37H + L43H + G45H) on the binding face — the sign flips (+0.836) but binding drops to 0.659. Centre: sr6-r37, the same design with position 37 reverted, which recovers binding (mouse 0.872, the project record) and loses most of the switch (+0.169). Right: sr2-ds2-mce-14-v7-v1-r2a, two histidines moved off the binding face (Q30H + E33H) — binding kept (0.843 / 0.860) with a +0.734 switch. The submitted champion is the single-substitution version of this last geometry.

The chain of reasoning, end to end:

  1. The mechanism is chosen from chemistry, not search. Histidine is the only residue whose charge changes across 6.0–7.4. Place it facing a positively charged target residue and you get: neutral at 7.4, the binder holds; protonated at 6.0, two positive charges repel, the binder leaves (submission/methodology.md).
  2. The target offers a usable cation site, and it survives mouse. The trio Arg103 / Lys112 on neighbouring protomers sits within 13 Å, and both positions keep their charge class in mouse (R103→K, K112→K). The neighbouring glutamates are a known screening risk and were recorded as such (notes/research-phase-0.md).
  3. The objective was measured before it was claimed. The linkage check found the lineage running the wrong way, −0.11 to −0.99 across five complexes. That negative is on the record in notes/linkage-check.md and in lineage.json, and it is the reason the retrofit exists.
  4. The first retrofit worked on paper and cost binding. Three histidines on the binding face: +0.836, but human confidence down to 0.659.
  5. The reversion scan found which histidine was expensive. H37. That gave both a recovered binder (sr6-r37) and the idea for the next step.
  6. Moving the switch off the binding face solved it. Histidines 7–9 Å from the interface cations, on positions 30 and 33 instead of 37/43/45. E33H alone converts a salt-bridge glutamate into the switch and reads +1.738 (54.7×) with human 0.849 and mouse 0.847 — a 0.007 cost against its no-switch parent.
  7. The honest limit. The scorer is rank-grade and measured conservative by about two orders of magnitude against its FcRn reference: FcRn, a known greater-than-100-fold real switch, scores −1.02 in this instrument (notes/submission-set-2026-10-18.md). 54.7× is also above every value the scorer produced in its own validation. So the readable parts are the sign and the relative ranking, not the fold number — and the paired controls exist so that the assay can measure the real one.

11. How the design serves objective 2: mouse cross-reactivity

  1. It was measured, not assumed. The mouse construct (P06804 85–235) was built by alignment from the human one and folded with the identical protocol. The first measurement showed a ~0.2 gap.
  2. It was then selected for. Mouse became the primary filter: 64 sequences designed toward the mouse-conserved contacts, 16 folded on mouse, one hit (mce-14, mouse 0.847). Human retention was confirmed on the same molecule afterwards (0.852).
  3. Both dual-select generations kept both reads in the loop simultaneously, which is how ds-mce-14-v6 came out better than its parent on both targets and how the mouse record (0.868) was set.
  4. The visual check agreed. Headless Mol* renders of mce-14 on both species show the same pose: an elongated helical element along the trimer edge, a continuous contact band on one face, 38 interface residues on mouse and 40 on human, contacting two protomers in both cases, with the engaged binder positions nearly identical (7–46 on both) (notes/views-review-mce14.md).
  5. The limit, stated plainly. "Cross-reactivity here means co-fold confidence at the designed site on both species, nothing more" (notes/submission-set-2026-10-18.md). It is not a measured cross-species affinity, and the calibration dataset's own warning applies: among released designs, only the tightest human binders bound mouse at all.

Three findings, all recorded as they came: nothing in the submission is structurally implausible (pTM 0.93–0.96, 67–77 of buried surface in BoltzGen's own units); the ranking disagrees with ours — BoltzGen puts r2a first and our lead r2c fifth, and neither metric is ground truth, so both views stay represented in the submitted set; and zero PLIP hydrogen bonds on every design — the family binds through a hydrophobic helix-bundle interface, consistent with the scaffold's composition.

13. What is honest and what is not yet known

  • Nothing here is wet-lab validated. There is no assay data for any design in this project. Every number above is a structure prediction or a score computed from one.
  • The submitted designs are not on the brief's recommended epitope. They sit on the released problem's B102/D62 two-protomer junction. The two campaigns aimed explicitly at the receptor-binding junction — X3-A (A83, A87, A89, B147) and RBS batch-03 — both produced zero designs that clear the bar and sit on the designed site, under the fixed protocol. notes/genie3-round2-family.md names the productive surface "the benchmark's groove-adjacent surface" and states the conclusion: epitope difficulty gates everything. The records do not map the released problem's B102/D62 into 1TNF numbering, so this document cannot state how far apart the two sites actually are.
  • The switch magnitude is the weakest claim in the set. The scorer is rank-grade, conservative by roughly two orders against its own FcRn reference, and 54.7× is above every value it produced in validation. The sign is the result; the paired controls exist precisely so the assay can supply the number.
  • Cross-reactivity means co-fold confidence on both species. Nothing in this project measures a cross-species affinity ratio.
  • The main metric is rank-grade, by measurement. In the calibration, three never-bound released designs outscored every wet-lab winner, and a real 2.1 nM binder scored 0.06. The ≥ 0.8 band bound about 26 % of the time. "Promising" is the strongest word the evidence supports.
  • The campaign is narrow by construction. All eight submitted designs are the same 64-residue backbone and the same helical fold. Mining-02 looked for a third family and found none; the d12 family failed mouse. A single-scaffold submission has a single-scaffold failure mode.
  • pDockQ2 was never satisfied by the submitted family. The d7 lineage reads 0.08–0.18 on the pose leg, well under the 0.23 of the original bar. That leg was dropped on calibration evidence, not because the designs passed it.
  • Zero predicted hydrogen bonds at the interface across all eight designs (BoltzGen/PLIP). Expected for a hydrophobic helix-bundle interface, but it is a real developability note.
  • Negatives are kept, not buried. The RFdiffusion3 campaign, the BoltzGen X1 zero, the CA-only sequencing trap, the inverted natural linkage, the sr3/sr4 recovery collapse, the two mining plateaus and the RBS negative are all on the record in lineage.json and notes/. The fold outputs were pruned on 2026-10-18 (229 directories deleted, 3.19 GB) but every deleted design's sequence is archived in notes/genie3/archive-all-designs.csv and its scores remain in notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv (notes/genie3/CLEANUP-2026-10-18.md).

Three places where this challenge's own records disagree, flagged here rather than silently resolved:

  1. notes/submission-set-2026-10-18.md lists ds-mce-14-v6 as "human 0.854 / mouse 0.856". The primary records — lineage.json, notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv (the human-stage dsh- row reads 0.856, the mouse-stage ds- row 0.854) and the committed viewer page — all read human 0.856 / mouse 0.854. The two species are swapped in that one line of the note; this document follows the primary records.
  2. lineage.json records per-design pdockq2 values around 0.82 for the Genie 3 designs (e.g. 0.8263 for e1b-d7x-t3-3-v6), while notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv reads 0.121–0.181 for the same five folds. The screen CSV is the pDockQ2 record used throughout this document; the lineage field looks like a different quantity carrying the wrong label.
  3. lineage.json names the best round-1 switch mutant as "G45H + L37H + S48H", but the submitted sr1-mce-14-b sequence differs from mce-14 at positions 37, 43 and 45 (L37H, L43H, G45H), and position 48 is unchanged. The lineage phrase describes the c-class variant that scored +0.877 and then lost mouse; the b-class that was submitted is the 37/43/45 version. The submitted CSV is the authority for what the sequence is.

Two further gaps worth naming: the mouse-score range quoted in notes/lineage-best-design.md ("0.46–0.64") does not cover the measured spread of the five mouse-check folds (0.258–0.770 in notes/genie3/genie3-all-scores.csv), and no record in this tree maps our eight design names onto the Proteinbase ids shown on the submission page (crimson-swan-quartz, gentle-raven-ivy, noble-ram-granite, golden-ram-willow, silver-mole-bronze, calm-dove-leaf, …) — the README states that mapping is still to be confirmed.
